Ana R.: FYI — FinCo asked for an 18-month pin on model `redwood-v2` citing regulatory audit windows. We need a plan: product tradeoffs, infra cost, and a migration runway. Thoughts?

Mike C.: 18mo seems excessive as a default. Proposal: 6mo default TTL, with an enterprise opt-in for extended pins tied to reserved capacity or a fee. That lets us limit resource churn. @Sophia?

Sophia P.: Agree 18mo is heavy. Tech notes: `redwood-v2` uses the old KV layout and prevents some memory optimizations. Keeping it pinned increases GPU-hosted RAM by ~25% for pinned capacity and complicates kernel upgrades. Ballpark additional infra: ~$0.08/1000 tokens/day per 10k active users pinned.

Jordan L.: From product side we should formalize launch/migration criteria and a "soft-landing" deprecation window. Minimal checklist idea:
- compatibility score >= 90% on customer prompt corpus (automated evals)
- latency regression < 5% vs pinned baseline
- canary at 5% of traffic for 2 weeks with rollback signal
- documented fallback policy (auto-route to pinned model if mismatch)

Ana R.: I'm drafting a migration SLA and runbook. Quick config example for pin policy (for engineering):
```yaml
pin_policy:
  default_ttl_days: 180
  enterprise_ttl_days: 540
  grace_period_days: 30  # extra time for customer opt-in and data migration
  canary:
    percent: 5
    duration_days: 14
  rollback_signal:
    eval_fail_rate_pct: 5
    latency_regression_pct: 10
```

Mike C.: That YAML looks good. Can we add a cost signal so sales can quote? e.g., `cost_surcharge_pct` for extended pins. Also need UI surface in Console for pin requests and expiration reminders.

Sophia P.: We can compute a per-customer surcharge once we have their qps and prompt distribution. I can attach a small calc in the runbook. Also engineering ask: if we allow long pins, we need a periodic compatibility smoke test that runs against pinned models to detect silent degrads.

Jordan L.: Decision items for this thread: 1) default TTL = 180 days, 2) enterprise option up to 540 days with surcharge, 3) require compatibility >=90% and canary rollout gates, 4) add a graceful fallback route and monthly smoke tests. Anyone object?

Ana R.: No objections from product. Action items: 
- @Mike C. -> spec Console changes + sales flow (due EOD next Tue)
- @Sophia P. -> infra cost calc + periodic smoke test design (due Fri)
- @Jordan L. -> migration runbook + compatibility eval harness (due next Wed)

catalog-bot: New runbook ticket created: #RUNBOOK-842

Mike C.: Noted, I'll start the Console mockups. Quick Q: do we want a checkbox for "opt-in extended pin (enterprise)" or a formal contract flow?

Ana R.: Formal contract + Console request for tracking. Console checkbox triggers a sales ticket. Keeps audit + billing clean.

Sophia P.: One more infra note: add a TTL metric to the model catalog dashboard so SRE can monitor pinned capacity over time.

Jordan L.: I'll include a migration timeline template in the runbook (canary weeks, communication cadence, customer opt-in steps).

Ana R.: OK, agreed. We'll present this at next roadmap review. If nothing changes, default TTL=180d and enterprise path enabled. Closing here — follow-ups in #RUNBOOK-842. :thumbsup:
